title: How the day closed
text: Stocks fell for a second day in a row. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) lost about 1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) lost about 0.7%. Most big tech names slipped, while industrial and health companies held up better. Everyone is now waiting for NVIDIA's report, which comes out after the close tonight. Nothing on this page is advice; it is here to help us learn.

title: NVIDIA reports tonight, near its lowest price of the year
text: NVIDIA closed at $155.46, down 0.4%. That is only 7% of the way up from its lowest price of the past year, and 36% below its high. Its results come out after 4 pm New York time, so tomorrow's price can jump or drop a lot. Its suppliers and partners (AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv) often move with it.

title: TSMC and Microsoft led the drop on our list
text: TSMC fell 3.7% and Microsoft fell 2.3%, two of the bigger drops on our list. Broadcom went the other way and rose 2.5%. When stocks in the same group move in different directions, it reminds us that each company has its own story.

title: Alphabet sits close to its one year low
text: Alphabet closed at $280.20, very close to its lowest price of the past year ($272.11). Anthropic, an AI company that Alphabet has invested in, plans to set its stock price this week. That event could change how investors feel about Alphabet.

title: Rocket Lab keeps the top risk score
text: Rocket Lab fell 4.0% and has a risk score of 10 out of 10. It is 63% below its high of the past year. A high score means the price swings a lot, so even a small amount of money in it can go up or down fast.

title: Lesson 55: What is a defensive stock?
text: A defensive stock belongs to a company that people keep paying even when times are hard, like medicine, electricity, food, or national defense. Because their sales do not drop much in a slow economy, these stocks often fall less when the market is scared. Today is a good example: most groups fell, but health and industrial companies held up better, and Lockheed Martin rose 0.9%. Defensive does not mean safe; these stocks can still fall. They just tend to move more calmly, which is why many investors keep some of them to balance riskier picks.

title: Where today's numbers come from
text: Prices are the close of Tuesday, November 17, 2026, from Financial Modeling Prep. Analyst price targets cover NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE. The 10 year Treasury rate is a monthly average from Alpha Vantage. NVIDIA's results are not included yet, because they come out after this update. News comes from web searches, and we only used facts we could check.
